headline: Cloud revenue more than doubles as AI demand lifts growth
summary_short: Revenue rose 25% to $127.6B and Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7B. Operating income grew 30% to $40.6B, but EPS fell to $2.12 from $2.87 on an $8.7B equity securities loss.
summary_long: Operating margin was 31.8%. Google Cloud operating income more than tripled to $11.1B. Search query growth was the highest in five years. Other income swung to a $8.2B loss from a $12.8B gain, with a $0.55 per share hit from equity securities. Capex of $51.4B compares with $24.0B a year earlier. Alphabet issued $28.7B of senior notes and repurchased no stock; the quarterly common dividend is $0.22.
confidence_notes: EPS delta and capex delta are computed from the release's year-ago comparatives. Net income is after $298M of preferred dividends. TPU systems sales are cited as a meaningful contributor to Cloud growth. GOOG and GOOGL share one release.

drivers.explanation: Strong growth in Google Cloud Platform across enterprise AI infrastructure, enterprise AI solutions and core services; TPU systems sales were a meaningful contributor.
AI investments are driving overall query growth, including commercial queries; year-over-year query growth is the highest in five years.
Net loss on equity securities of $8.7 billion cut diluted EPS by $0.55, against a large gain in the year-ago quarter's other income.
CEO says full-stack AI approach is driving momentum and Alphabet is on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate.
